title: Counter E-Receipt Kiosk
tagline: Customers scan a counter QR, type their tax ID, and get a Revenue Dept e-Tax Invoice in LINE in 30 seconds
problem: Every Easy E-Receipt round (up to 50,000 baht of personal tax deduction) only counts e-Tax Invoices or e-Receipts issued through the Revenue Department system, so shoppers at small VAT-registered shops now ask for a full electronic tax invoice at the counter. Owners of cafes, pharmacies, gadget and hardware shops still write paper invoices or retype buyer details into FlowAccount or PEAK after closing, which takes 3-5 minutes per request and produces typos in tax IDs and branch codes that void the deduction. Accounting suites are built for the back office, not for a queue of customers at a till, and sellers who miss the rush lose sales to chains that issue e-receipts instantly.
solution: A LINE LIFF mini-app plus a printed counter QR: the customer scans, enters their 13-digit tax ID once (saved to their LINE profile with consent), and the cashier taps the matching sale on a phone. The app validates the tax ID checksum and branch code, builds the invoice, and issues it through the e-Tax Invoice by Time Stamp route (businesses under 30M baht revenue) or via an INET-style service provider for larger shops, then pushes the PDF back into the customer's LINE chat. It syncs every issued document to FlowAccount or PEAK via API or CSV so the bookkeeper is not double-entering, and produces the monthly output-VAT report. Unlike accounting suites, the flow is designed for a 30-second counter interaction, works on the shop's existing POS or with no POS at all, and spikes cheaply for campaign seasons with a per-document top-up.
target_audience: VAT-registered retail shops under 30M baht revenue; cafes and restaurants in malls; pharmacies and clinics; gadget, hardware and bookshops during Easy E-Receipt campaigns
pricing: Free 20 e-receipts/month; Shop ฿290/month (300 docs); Multi-branch ฿790/month; top-up ฿1 per extra document
score_justification: L3 mostly workflow, light OCR of buyer docs; E4 LIFF + Time Stamp email flow in 3-4 wks; A4 Easy E-Receipt drives yearly demand; P4 LINE OA + accountant referrals; M2 customer tax-ID vault is modest; W4 shops already pay FlowAccount/PEAK
platform_distribution: LINE OA + LIFF; bookkeeping-firm referrals; Facebook seller groups during Easy E-Receipt season
tam_source: bottom-up: ~320,000 small VAT-registered retailers (est.) x ฿290/month x 12
competitors: FlowAccount; PEAK; INET e-Tax service; paper tax invoice books
competitor_gap: FlowAccount and PEAK support e-Tax by Time Stamp but assume back-office entry; none offer a customer-self-serve counter QR that captures buyer tax details at the till
demand_evidence: Easy E-Receipt ran in 2567 and 2568 and a 2569 round is reported, each time restricted to e-Tax Invoice/e-Receipt documents; PEAK and FlowAccount both publish e-Tax by Time Stamp guides, showing SME demand.
source_urls: https://www.thairath.co.th/money/economics/thai_economics/2752861 | https://www.bangkokbiznews.com/finance/investment/1107179 | https://www.rd.go.th/region/04/saraburi/85/5202.html | https://flowaccount.com/en/our-integrations/etax-by-email | https://intercom.help/peak/en/articles/8764369-คำถามที-พบบ-อยเกี-ยวกับ-e-tax-invoice-faq012 | https://www.fiscal-requirements.com/news/5729
unique_data_capture: Opt-in buyer tax-profile vault reused across every participating shop, plus seasonal e-receipt volume by category
commoditization_risk: Medium: FlowAccount or LINE MyShop could add a counter QR flow, but they have not prioritised the till use case
regulatory_notes: Must follow Revenue Department e-Tax Invoice by Time Stamp rules (revenue cap 30M baht, approved email); buyer tax IDs are personal data under PDPA, needing consent and a DPA with merchants
founder_feasibility: Offshore SaaS sold to Thai merchants needs no Thai entity; a foreign-majority Thai company providing the service falls under FBA List 3 (services) and needs a Foreign Business Licence or BOI 5.10 digital promotion (which allows 100% foreign ownership), otherwise a 51% Thai-held structure. Solo founder can ship it; a Thai co-founder or bookkeeper partner helps with Revenue Department registration support. PDPA: merchant is controller, the app is processor.
mvp_features: Counter QR + LIFF form with tax-ID checksum; e-Tax by Time Stamp issuance; PDF return to customer LINE chat; FlowAccount/PEAK sync; monthly output-VAT report; campaign-season top-ups
tech_stack: LINE LIFF + Next.js + Supabase + Revenue Dept Time Stamp email flow + PDF generator
review_notes: Depends on the Easy E-Receipt campaign recurring each year; demand outside campaign months is unproven.

title: PromptPay Match Ledger
tagline: Auto-matches every PromptPay credit in your bank feed to the LINE or Facebook order it paid for
problem: Thai social sellers and small shops take most payments by PromptPay transfer: the country processed roughly 24 billion PromptPay transactions in 2024 and more than 2 billion a month in 2025. Each payment arrives as a bare bank notification with an amount and a truncated name, while the order sits in a LINE chat or Facebook comment thread, so staff spend an hour a day scrolling bank apps to tick off who paid. Duplicate amounts (many orders cost 299 baht) cause shipping to the wrong buyer, and missed partial payments are only discovered at month-end when the bookkeeper cannot reconcile the account. Slip-check bots verify that a slip is real, but they do not tell you which order it belongs to or whether the money actually landed.
solution: A reconciliation ledger that ingests bank credits from business-account statement exports, bank notification emails or merchant-QR settlement files and matches them to open orders captured from LINE OA, Facebook Pages, or a simple order sheet. Matching uses amount, time window, payer-name fuzzy match in Thai and English, and unique-satang tricks (the app tells each buyer to pay 299.13 instead of 299) so that identical prices never collide. Unmatched credits and unpaid orders appear in a daily LINE digest with one-tap actions to nudge the buyer or mark partial payment. Month-end it exports a reconciled sales ledger to FlowAccount or PEAK, which is the step slip checkers and bank apps skip entirely.
target_audience: LINE and Facebook social sellers; Instagram boutiques; small wholesalers taking PromptPay; bookkeepers serving online sellers
business_model: Subscription tiered by monthly matched transactions
pricing: Starter ฿199/month (500 matches); Pro ฿590/month (3,000 matches); Bookkeeper ฿1,490/month (10 client shops)
score_justification: L3 fuzzy matching + LLM name parsing; E3 bank-export parsers per bank take 6-8 wks; A4 PromptPay is the default rail; P3 Facebook seller groups + bookkeepers; M4 payer-to-customer identity graph compounds; W4 sellers already pay slip bots and Zort
platform_distribution: LINE OA; Thai online-seller Facebook groups; bookkeeping-firm partnerships; TikTok tutorials
tam_source: bottom-up: ~400,000 active social sellers (est.) x ฿290 average/month x 12
competitors: SlipOK; K SHOP merchant app (KBank); Zort; Page365
competitor_gap: Slip bots verify authenticity only; bank merchant apps show credits but not orders; order tools like Zort track orders but do not reconcile bank credits to them
demand_evidence: PromptPay processed about 24.3 billion transactions in 2024 and over 2.5 billion in March 2026 alone; regulators keep telling sellers to check money in the account rather than trust slips, which is exactly the reconciliation step.
unique_data_capture: Payer-name to customer identity graph across shops and banks, improving match rates and later powering fraud flags
commoditization_risk: Medium: banks could add order tagging to merchant QR apps, but each bank only sees its own account
regulatory_notes: Read-only use of statements, never holds funds, so no BOT e-payment licence; bank credentials must not be stored (use exports or email forwarding); PDPA consent for payer names
founder_feasibility: Offshore SaaS sold to Thai merchants needs no Thai entity; a foreign-majority Thai company providing the service falls under FBA List 3 (services) and needs a Foreign Business Licence or BOI 5.10 digital promotion (which allows 100% foreign ownership), otherwise a 51% Thai-held structure. Solo technical founder feasible; per-bank parsers are the grind. Avoid screen-scraping bank apps to stay clear of bank terms.
mvp_features: Bank statement/email ingestion for 5 major banks; unique-satang payment amounts; LINE/Facebook order capture; fuzzy Thai-name matcher; daily unpaid/unmatched LINE digest; FlowAccount/PEAK export
tech_stack: Next.js + Supabase + LINE Messaging API + Meta Graph API + LLM API (Claude/GPT) for Thai name parsing
review_notes: Open question: how many sellers will forward bank emails or exports reliably; Page365 and K SHOP feature sets were not verified directly in this research pass.

title: Fifty Tawi Tracker
tagline: Chases, checks and files 50 Tawi withholding-tax certificates so freelancers reclaim every baht
problem: When Thai companies pay a freelancer or a small supplier, they withhold 3% (or 1-5% by type) and must hand over a 50 Tawi certificate, then file PND 3 or PND 53 by the 7th of the next month. Recipients routinely chase clients for months to get the certificate, and without it they cannot offset the withheld tax in their annual return, so money is simply left with the Revenue Department. Payers who are tiny companies juggle certificates in Excel, mix up PND 3 versus PND 53, and pay surcharges for late filing. The e-Withholding Tax system via banks removes the paper only when both sides use a participating bank channel, which most small payers do not.
solution: Two sides in one product. For recipients (freelancers, expat consultants, small agencies) it reads invoices and payment credits, predicts which payments should carry withholding, and automatically chases the payer by email or LINE until a 50 Tawi arrives; OCR then checks amounts, tax IDs and PND type against the invoice. For payers it generates compliant 50 Tawi PDFs in Thai and English, sends them, and pre-fills PND 3 and PND 53 attachment files for e-Filing. A year-end view totals withheld tax per client for PND 90/91 or PND 50, which is where the money is recovered. Accounting suites generate certificates for the payer but nobody manages the recipient chase, which is the painful half.
target_audience: Thai freelancers and creators; expat consultants and teachers paid as contractors; small agencies; micro-companies paying contractors
pricing: Free 5 certificates/year; Freelancer ฿990/year; Company ฿350/month (unlimited PND 3/53 prep)
score_justification: L4 OCR + LLM classifies withholding and drafts chasers; E4 4 wks; A3 constant evergreen search interest, few loud threads found; P3 freelancer FB groups and accountant partners; M3 payer reliability data; W3 freelancers price-sensitive, companies pay
platform_distribution: LINE OA; Thai freelancer Facebook groups; Pantip Sinthorn tax threads in Q1 filing season; Google SEO for 50 ทวิ queries
tam_source: bottom-up: 500,000 freelancers x ฿990/yr + 30,000 micro-companies x ฿4,200/yr (est.)
competitors: FlowAccount; PEAK; Revenue Department e-Withholding Tax via banks; Excel
competitor_gap: Suites issue certificates for payers but no tool chases missing certificates on the recipient side or reconciles them to the annual return
demand_evidence: FlowAccount and PEAK both publish explainer content on PND 3 vs PND 53 and sending 50 Tawi, and the Revenue Department built e-Withholding Tax with 11 banks specifically to reduce this paperwork.
source_urls: https://flowaccount.com/blog/ภ-ง-ด-3-หัก-ณ-ที่จ่าย/ | https://www.bangkokbank.com/th-TH/Business-Banking/Manage-My-Business/Payments/eWithholding-Tax | https://media.thaigov.go.th/uploads/document/142/2020/10/pdf/Doc_20201027132922000000.pdf | https://flowaccount.com/pricing
unique_data_capture: Dataset of which payers issue certificates late or wrong, building a payer-reliability score and auto-classification of withholding rates by service type
commoditization_risk: Medium: wider e-Withholding Tax adoption would shrink paper certificates, though small payers lag
regulatory_notes: Tax preparation help is fine; filing on a client's behalf needs a licensed accountant or tax auditor partner; PDPA covers tax IDs and income data
founder_feasibility: Offshore SaaS sold to Thai merchants needs no Thai entity; a foreign-majority Thai company providing the service falls under FBA List 3 (services) and needs a Foreign Business Licence or BOI 5.10 digital promotion (which allows 100% foreign ownership), otherwise a 51% Thai-held structure. Foreign founder fine as software; partner with a Thai licensed bookkeeper for any filing service. English UI is a selling point for expat contractors.
mvp_features: Invoice and bank-credit import; withholding predictor; auto-chaser via email/LINE; 50 Tawi OCR and validation; PND 3/53 attachment export; year-end withheld-tax summary
tech_stack: Next.js + Supabase + OCR + LLM API (Claude/GPT) + LINE Messaging API
review_notes: Risk that e-Withholding Tax adoption accelerates and removes the certificate chase for larger payers.

title: Marketplace Fee Auditor
tagline: Audits every Shopee, Lazada and TikTok Shop payout for fee errors and builds your input-VAT schedule
problem: Thai marketplace sellers now pay stacked fees: Shopee commissions of roughly 7.5-17% plus a 3.21% transaction fee and 5-8.5% programme service fees, Lazada and TikTok Shop with their own commission, payment and growth fees, all changing several times a year. Payout reports differ per platform, deductions are netted, and fees are calculated on bases sellers cannot easily check, so many sellers only discover they are unprofitable on a SKU months later. Bookkeepers also need the platforms' monthly tax invoices to claim input VAT on those fees, and assembling them across three seller centres is manual. Order-management tools like Zort and BigSeller sync stock and orders, but they do not audit fees against the published rate card.
solution: The app connects to Shopee, Lazada and TikTok Shop seller APIs (or ingests their payout exports) and recomputes every order's expected fees from a maintained rate card by category, programme and payment method. Discrepancies such as fees charged on cancelled orders, wrong category rates or duplicated programme fees are flagged with an evidence pack ready for a seller-centre ticket. A true-margin dashboard shows net profit per SKU per platform after all fees, ads and shipping subsidies, and simulates fee changes before they go live. At month-end it collects each platform's fee tax invoices and outputs an input-VAT schedule and journal for FlowAccount or PEAK, closing the loop no OMS covers.
target_audience: Shopee/Lazada/TikTok Shop sellers doing ฿100k-฿5M per month; e-commerce bookkeepers; brand distributors
pricing: Lite ฿390/month (<฿300k GMV); Growth ฿990/month; Agency ฿2,990/month (10 shops)
score_justification: L3 rules engine + LLM for reading fee notices; E3 three API integrations, 8 wks; A4 repeated fee-hike news and seller anger; P3 seller FB groups + bookkeepers; M4 fee-discrepancy dataset across sellers; W4 sellers already pay OMS tools
platform_distribution: Thai seller Facebook groups; TikTok seller education creators; bookkeeping-firm partnerships; Shopee/Lazada open-platform app listings
tam_source: bottom-up: ~120,000 sellers above ฿100k GMV/month (est.) x ฿600/month x 12
competitors: Zort; BigSeller; FlowAccount marketplace integration; spreadsheets
competitor_gap: OMS tools sync orders and stock but none recompute fees against the official rate card or build the input-VAT schedule from platform fee invoices
demand_evidence: Bangkok Post and seller blogs report repeated Shopee and Lazada commission increases (Shopee Thailand up to 13% in 2024, a base-rate rise in Nov 2025, new fees in 2026); FlowAccount maintains a 2026 fee-update article because sellers search for it.
unique_data_capture: Cross-seller dataset of fee discrepancies and true margins by category, which becomes a benchmark product and powers early warnings when platforms change fees
commoditization_risk: Medium: platforms will not audit themselves, but OMS vendors could add fee recalculation
regulatory_notes: Use official open-platform APIs and seller consent; PDPA covers buyer data in order exports (minimise and hash)
founder_feasibility: Offshore SaaS sold to Thai merchants needs no Thai entity; a foreign-majority Thai company providing the service falls under FBA List 3 (services) and needs a Foreign Business Licence or BOI 5.10 digital promotion (which allows 100% foreign ownership), otherwise a 51% Thai-held structure. Solo founder feasible if comfortable maintaining three APIs; a Thai co-founder helps with platform partner programmes.
mvp_features: Payout import for 3 marketplaces; rate-card fee recalculation; discrepancy evidence pack; SKU true-margin dashboard; fee-change simulator; input-VAT schedule export
tech_stack: Next.js + Postgres + Shopee/Lazada/TikTok Shop open APIs + LLM API (Claude/GPT) for fee-notice parsing
review_notes: Biggest risk is API access and rate-card maintenance as platforms change fees several times a year; exact 2026 rates need verification in each seller centre.

title: Small Crew Payroll
tagline: Payroll, Social Security and PND 1 for 1-30 staff, with payslips in Thai, Burmese and English via LINE
problem: Every Thai employer with even one employee must register with the Social Security Office within 30 days and remit 5% contributions monthly, and from January 2026 the wage ceiling rose from 15,000 to 17,500 baht (max 875 baht a month), with further steps in 2029 and 2032. Small restaurants, salons and shops often run payroll in Excel, miss the new cap, and file the SSO e-Service upload and PND 1 manually, while migrant staff from Myanmar, Laos and Cambodia need payslips they can read and SSO registration tied to work-permit renewals. Enterprise payroll vendors like Humanica and Prosoft HRMI target mid-to-large firms with quote-based pricing, so micro-employers are left with spreadsheets and agents. Mistakes lead to surcharges and to staff losing SSO benefits they paid for.
solution: A mobile-first payroll for 1-30 staff: enter wages, overtime, advances and deductions, and the app calculates SSO contributions with the current ceiling table, PND 1 withholding, and net pay. It generates the SSO e-Service contribution file and PND 1 attachment for upload, reminds the owner before the 15th, and can produce a PromptPay bulk-pay list. Each employee receives a payslip in Thai, Burmese, Lao, Khmer or English through LINE, and the app tracks migrant workers' work-permit and SSO registration expiry so renewals are not missed. It is priced per head for micro-employers, unlike enterprise HRIS, and updates statutory tables automatically when rates change.
target_audience: Restaurants and street-food shops with staff; salons and spas; retail shops; expat-owned small companies; employers of migrant workers
pricing: ฿39 per employee/month (min ฿190); migrant-worker document tracking +฿20/employee
score_justification: L3 calculation + translation, AI light; E3 statutory logic + file formats, 6-8 wks; A4 SSO ceiling change made 2026 headlines; P3 LINE OA + bookkeepers + employer networks; M3 wage benchmarks by sector; W4 employers already pay agents and accountants
platform_distribution: LINE OA; restaurant-owner Facebook groups; bookkeeping firms; migrant-worker recruitment agencies
tam_source: bottom-up: ~700,000 employers with 1-30 staff (est.) x 6 staff x ฿39 x 12 x 50% reachable
competitors: Humanica; HumanSoft; Prosoft HRMI; FlowAccount payroll; Excel and payroll agents
competitor_gap: Incumbents are quote-based and built for HR departments; none combine per-head micro pricing, multilingual payslips over LINE and migrant work-permit tracking
demand_evidence: Cabinet approved raising the SSO wage ceiling to 17,500 baht from 1 January 2026, widely covered by Thairath, Krungsri and PEAK help articles; employers were told to renew migrant work permits by 31 March 2026, with small employers reporting the registration process is too complicated.
unique_data_capture: Anonymised wage, overtime and turnover benchmarks for micro-employers by sector and province
commoditization_risk: Medium: FlowAccount or PEAK could deepen payroll, but multilingual migrant support is a niche they ignore
regulatory_notes: Payroll data is sensitive personal data under PDPA; the app prepares files but the employer submits to SSO; must track statutory changes (ceiling steps in 2029/2032)
founder_feasibility: Offshore SaaS sold to Thai merchants needs no Thai entity; a foreign-majority Thai company providing the service falls under FBA List 3 (services) and needs a Foreign Business Licence or BOI 5.10 digital promotion (which allows 100% foreign ownership), otherwise a 51% Thai-held structure. Feasible solo with a Thai payroll-accountant advisor to sign off rules; do not act as employer-of-record (that needs a Thai entity).
payment_rails: PromptPay QR + cards (Omise); PromptPay bulk-pay list export
mvp_features: Payroll calculator with SSO/PND 1 tables; SSO e-Service upload file; PND 1 attachment export; multilingual LINE payslips; work-permit and SSO expiry tracker; due-date reminders
tech_stack: Next.js + Supabase + LINE Messaging API + PDF generation + LLM API (Claude/GPT) for payslip translation
review_notes: Distribution to micro-employers is the hard part; verify SSO e-Service file format stability before building.

title: LINE Deposit Booking
tagline: LINE mini-app booking with PromptPay deposits that cuts no-shows for salons, clinics and massage shops
problem: Thai salons, nail studios, massage shops and small clinics take bookings by LINE chat, which means owners answer the same availability questions dozens of times a day and keep the calendar in their head or a paper book. No-shows are common because nothing is prepaid, and asking for a deposit by sending a PromptPay number and then checking slips by hand is awkward and error-prone. Foreign residents and tourists often cannot book at all because staff reply only in Thai. Global booking apps require customers to download another app, which Thai customers who live in LINE will not do.
solution: A booking mini-app that runs inside the shop's LINE OA: customers pick a service, staff member and slot, pay a deposit by dynamic PromptPay QR, and the payment is confirmed automatically rather than by slip photo. Reminders go out through LINE 24 hours and 2 hours before, and late cancellations keep the deposit according to the shop's policy, which is shown in Thai and English. Staff get a simple day view and can block slots from their phone; the owner gets no-show, utilisation and repeat-visit reports. Because it lives inside LINE and uses LINE login, there is no app download, which is the key advantage over global booking platforms. This adapts the generic booking idea in the corpus (IDEA-053) to LINE and PromptPay deposits.
target_audience: Hair and nail salons; massage and spa shops; aesthetic and dental clinics; tattoo studios; fitness and Muay Thai trainers
pricing: Solo ฿350/month; Shop ฿790/month (up to 8 staff); deposit processing at gateway cost + ฿2/booking
score_justification: L2 mostly software, AI only for chat FAQ; E4 LIFF booking in 4 wks; A4 LINE is the default booking channel; P4 LINE OA distribution and salon networks; M3 no-show and demand data by area; W4 salons pay for POS and LINE OA plans
platform_distribution: LINE OA / LINE MINI App directory; salon supply distributors; Facebook groups for salon owners
tam_source: bottom-up: ~120,000 appointment-based small businesses (est.) x ฿500/month x 12
competitors: LINE OA chat and manual booking; Fresha; Wongnai Beauty booking; Google Calendar
competitor_gap: Global tools need an app download and card payments; LINE OA lacks deposit-backed scheduling with automatic PromptPay confirmation
demand_evidence: LINE reports 56 million Thai users and over 12 billion Official Account conversations in 2025, and MINI App volume tripled after developer access opened in March 2026.
unique_data_capture: Area-level demand, no-show and price data for beauty and wellness services
commoditization_risk: Medium: LINE could ship native booking (it is building MINI Apps), and Fresha is expanding
regulatory_notes: Holding deposits would need a BOT e-payment licence, so route funds directly to the merchant via a licensed gateway; health-clinic bookings involve sensitive data under PDPA
founder_feasibility: Offshore SaaS sold to Thai merchants needs no Thai entity; a foreign-majority Thai company providing the service falls under FBA List 3 (services) and needs a Foreign Business Licence or BOI 5.10 digital promotion (which allows 100% foreign ownership), otherwise a 51% Thai-held structure. Payment flow must use a licensed Thai gateway with funds settling to the merchant. Solo founder can build; field sales via salon distributors is helpful.

mvp_features: LIFF booking with staff/slot picker; PromptPay deposit with auto-confirmation; LINE reminders; cancellation policy engine; staff day view; no-show reports
tech_stack: LINE LIFF + Next.js + Supabase + payment gateway API
review_notes: Market adaptation of IDEA-053 BookingBuddy for LINE + PromptPay deposits; risk that LINE ships native booking.

title: Broadcast Budget Optimizer
tagline: Cuts LINE OA broadcast bills by sending the right message to the right friends, not to everyone
problem: LINE OA paid plans include a fixed message quota (for example 15,000 messages on the 1,200 baht Basic plan, with 0.08 baht per extra message, per the 2023 price change) and SMEs that broadcast to every friend burn through it in a couple of campaigns. LINE halved free broadcast messages and raised prices in 2023, which drew public backlash from small businesses, but most owners still blast the same promotion to the whole list because tagging friends manually is tedious. Blasting also drives blocks: every unwanted message pushes customers to block the account, shrinking the list the shop paid to build. LINE's own segmentation tools exist but require data most SMEs never capture.
solution: The tool connects to the shop's LINE OA via the Messaging API, captures purchase, chat and click events, and auto-tags friends by behaviour (bought in the last 30 days, browsed but never bought, dormant, VIP). Before each campaign it predicts reach, cost against the remaining quota and block risk, and recommends a narrowcast segment and send time. An AI assistant drafts the Thai copy and rich-menu variant for each segment, and A/B tests cheaply on small groups first. A monthly report shows baht saved versus whole-list broadcasting and block rate trends, tying the subscription directly to the LINE bill it reduces.
target_audience: SMEs on paid LINE OA plans; cafes and restaurant chains with large friend lists; beauty and fashion shops; LINE agencies managing many OAs
pricing: ฿490/month per OA; Agency ฿3,900/month (15 OAs)
score_justification: L3 segmentation + copy drafting; E4 Messaging API is well documented, 4 wks; A3 price-hike backlash but older; P4 LINE agency partners and OA owners; M3 behaviour-to-response data; W3 pays only if savings are visible
platform_distribution: LINE Marketplace/partner directory; LINE agencies; Marketing Oops and Facebook marketing groups
tam_source: bottom-up: ~80,000 SMEs on paid LINE OA plans (est.) x ฿490 x 12
competitors: LINE OA Manager built-in audiences; LINE agency CRM tools; Wongnai Reward Card
competitor_gap: Built-in audiences need manual tagging and offer no cost/block forecasting; agency CRMs are built for enterprises
demand_evidence: LINE's 2023 plan change cut free broadcast quota 50% and raised prices, criticised by Thai SMEs in KrASIA and Bangkok Post coverage; OA conversations reached 12 billion in 2025.
unique_data_capture: Segment-level response and block-rate data across many SMEs, used to benchmark send timing and message types
commoditization_risk: Medium: LINE can improve native audiences and AI targeting at any time, since it profits from messages but also from retention
regulatory_notes: Marketing messages require PDPA lawful basis/consent; must follow LINE platform development guidelines
founder_feasibility: Offshore SaaS sold to Thai merchants needs no Thai entity; a foreign-majority Thai company providing the service falls under FBA List 3 (services) and needs a Foreign Business Licence or BOI 5.10 digital promotion (which allows 100% foreign ownership), otherwise a 51% Thai-held structure. Solo founder feasible; becoming a LINE technology partner is easier with a Thai entity.
mvp_features: Messaging API event capture; auto-tagging; quota and cost forecaster; block-risk score; segment copy drafts; savings report
tech_stack: LINE Messaging API + Next.js + Supabase + LLM API (Claude/GPT)
review_notes: Current 2026 LINE OA plan prices were not verified; the cited quota figures date from the 2023 change.

title: Thai Shop Chat Agent
tagline: AI that answers Thai customer chats on LINE OA, takes orders and hands hard cases to the owner
problem: Thai SMEs sell through chat: LINE OA logged more than 12 billion conversations in 2025, and a shop owner may handle hundreds of questions a day about price, stock, sizes, delivery and payment, often at midnight. Slow replies lose sales to faster sellers, and hiring admins costs 12,000-15,000 baht a month each. Keyword chatbots break on informal Thai, slang and typos, and LINE's own AI auto-reply is generic and does not know the shop's live stock or order status. Foreign buyers who write in English get ignored.
solution: A LINE OA agent trained on the shop's catalogue, price list and policies, connected to stock in a sheet, Zort or the POS. It answers in natural Thai or English, quotes shipping, creates an order and a PromptPay QR, checks the payment, and posts a summary for the owner, escalating anything uncertain (complaints, custom orders) to a human with full context. The owner corrects answers in one tap and the agent learns the shop's tone and policies. The edge over generic chatbots is the live connection to stock and orders and a Thai-language evaluation set built from real seller chats.
target_audience: LINE and Facebook social sellers; small brands; clinics and beauty shops; tour and rental operators serving foreigners
pricing: Starter ฿690/month (1,000 chats); Pro ฿1,900/month (5,000 chats); overage ฿0.50/chat
score_justification: L5 AI does the core work; E4 4 wks with LLM API; A4 chat commerce is mainstream; P4 LINE OA; M2 chat logs are useful but rivals can collect the same; W4 cheaper than an admin salary
platform_distribution: LINE OA partner channel; TikTok demo videos; Facebook seller groups
tam_source: bottom-up: ~200,000 chat-heavy SMEs (est.) x ฿850/month x 12
competitors: LINE OA AI auto-reply; Zwiz.AI; LINE agency chatbot builders; hired admins
competitor_gap: Generic or rule-based bots lack live stock/order context and fluent informal Thai; agencies build one-off bots at project prices
demand_evidence: LINE OA hosts about 7 million accounts, 70% SMEs (secondary report), and chat commerce is described as a 23-billion-baht market; vendor guides on building AI chatbots for LINE OA are proliferating in 2026.

commoditization_risk: High: LINE ships native AI chat features and general assistants can be connected cheaply by agencies
regulatory_notes: PDPA consent for processing chats; disclose AI replies; avoid medical or financial advice for clinic clients

title: Thai Listing Localizer
tagline: Turns Chinese or English listings into native, compliant Thai TikTok Shop and Shopee listings
problem: Chinese factories, foreign brands and Thai importers listing on TikTok Shop and Shopee Thailand usually machine-translate titles and descriptions, producing stiff Thai that misses the search terms Thai shoppers actually type and reads as untrustworthy. Wrong claims words can also break Thai rules: cosmetics, supplements and food need Thai FDA-compliant wording, and electrical goods need TISI references. With cross-border goods flooding Thai marketplaces and Thai regulators pushing back, listings that look foreign and non-compliant are increasingly removed or ignored. Agencies charge per SKU and take days, which does not scale to catalogues of hundreds of products.
solution: Upload a catalogue (Chinese, English or rough Thai) and the tool rewrites each listing into natural marketplace Thai, using a keyword bank built from Thai search suggestions and best-selling listings in the category. A compliance checker flags banned or risky claims for FDA- and TISI-regulated categories and suggests compliant alternatives, and image-text translation replaces Chinese text on product images. It outputs platform-specific titles, bullet points and attributes in bulk files for TikTok Shop, Shopee and Lazada, plus an English version for expat buyers. It differs from generic translation by being keyword- and compliance-aware for Thailand specifically, which existing listing tools in the corpus (CLAUDE-201) do not focus on.

title: Thai Review Defect Radar
tagline: Mines Thai Shopee, Lazada and TikTok reviews to find the defects and size issues driving your returns
problem: Thai marketplace reviews are full of signal written in slang, emoji and abbreviations (for example complaints about size running small, smell, or courier damage) but sellers with hundreds of SKUs only read the one-star ones. Returns and refunds are expensive: TikTok Shop's No Longer Needed return option and platform-auto-approved refunds put the burden on sellers, and recurring defects keep generating returns. Thai sellers compete on price with a flood of imported goods, so a 1-2% return rate difference decides whether a SKU is profitable. Generic English review-analysis tools do not handle informal Thai well.
solution: The tool pulls reviews and return reasons from the seller's shops across three marketplaces and clusters them with a Thai-tuned model into defect themes (sizing, material, missing parts, packaging, courier, misleading photo). Each theme gets a trend line, affected SKUs, the cost in returns, and a suggested fix such as adding a size chart, changing a supplier or a listing photo. Competitor shops' public reviews can be tracked too, revealing weaknesses to exploit in listings. A weekly LINE summary keeps the owner on top of it; this is a Thai-language market adaptation of the generic review summariser in the corpus (IDEA-229).

title: Return Dispute Evidence Kit
tagline: Records every pack-out on video and auto-files evidence before TikTok Shop and Shopee dispute deadlines
problem: Thai sellers commonly face buyers who claim missing items, swapped goods or empty parcels, and platforms resolve many disputes on deadline: if a seller does not respond in time, TikTok Shop auto-approves the refund. Many Thai sellers already film themselves packing parcels as proof, but the clips sit on a phone and finding the right one for an order number days later is slow, so they miss the window. Returned items that come back damaged or are never returned must be appealed within about 15 days, another deadline that slips. Each lost dispute costs the item, shipping both ways and sometimes the shop's performance score.
solution: A phone or webcam app that starts recording when the packer scans the order's barcode, overlays order number, timestamp and SKU list on the video, and stops when the label is scanned. Clips are stored and indexed by order; when a return or dispute appears in the seller centre, the app pulls the clip, generates a still-frame evidence sheet and drafts the Thai appeal text, and alerts the owner on LINE well before the deadline. Return unboxing is recorded the same way to support claims for damaged or swapped returns. A dashboard shows disputes won, money recovered and buyers with repeat claims, which is evidence for platform abuse reports.
target_audience: Shopee/Lazada/TikTok Shop sellers shipping 50+ parcels a day; fulfilment warehouses; electronics and cosmetics sellers with high-value items

score_justification: L3 vision OCR + appeal drafting; E4 4-5 wks; A4 pack-video practice is widespread; P3 seller groups and fulfilment partners; M4 cross-seller serial-claimer data; W4 directly recovers money

demand_evidence: TikTok Shop guides document seller appeal windows (about 15 days for returned goods) and auto-approval when sellers do not respond; Thailand's competition regulator has mediated platform-seller disputes.

commoditization_risk: Low: platforms are not incentivised to build seller-side evidence tooling

title: Expat Company Compliance Desk
tagline: One bilingual calendar for every VAT, PND, SSO, work-permit and DBD filing a foreign-run Thai company owes
problem: Foreign founders running small Thai companies (restaurants, dive shops, agencies, BOI startups) face a stack of recurring obligations in Thai: monthly VAT PP30, PND 1/3/53, SSO contributions, annual financial statements to DBD, PND 50/51, work-permit and visa renewals, and Thai-staff ratio rules for work permits. Most rely on a single bookkeeper who emails Thai PDFs, and owners only learn of a missed deadline when a surcharge or a work-permit problem appears. Generic accounting apps assume a Thai-speaking user and do not cover immigration-linked deadlines. The cost is surcharges, frozen permits, and anxiety for owners who cannot read the notices.
solution: The owner answers a short onboarding (VAT status, staff count, BOI status, visa types), and the app builds a company-specific compliance calendar in English and Thai with every recurring deadline. Each item has a plain-English explanation, the responsible person (owner, bookkeeper, lawyer), and status; bookkeepers get a portal to upload filed receipts so the owner sees proof. Thai government letters and bookkeeper PDFs can be photographed and are translated and summarised, with any new deadline extracted. A marketplace of vetted bilingual bookkeepers and lawyers gives an exit when the owner needs help, earning referral fees.

title: Delivery GP Splitter
tagline: True margin per dish on Grab, LINE MAN, ShopeeFood and Robinhood, with per-app menu prices
problem: Thai restaurants pay GP commissions of roughly 15-30% on GrabFood and LINE MAN, plus 7% VAT on the fee, and rates change with campaigns: under Thai Chuay Thai Plus Grab offered 9%, LINE MAN 10-15%, ShopeeFood 13% and Robinhood 10.5%, with rules forcing merchants to choose a single platform. Owners rarely know which platform, menu item or promotion actually makes money after GP, VAT, packaging (container prices doubled in 2026) and co-funded discounts. Each platform's payout report has a different format, so most owners guess, mark up all menus by the same amount, and lose either margin or volume. Delivery aggregators focus on order intake, not profitability.
solution: The owner uploads or connects payout reports from each delivery app, and the tool rebuilds per-order economics: menu price, GP, VAT on GP, promo co-funding, packaging and food cost. It recommends platform-specific menu prices and bundles that hit a target margin, models what happens if the shop joins a campaign or switches platform, and flags orders where deductions do not match the contract rate. A daily LINE summary shows profit by platform, and a calculator helps owners respond to new GP offers within hours rather than weeks. This is a multi-platform Thai version of the Grab-only merchant ideas in the corpus (CLAUDE-210, CLAUDE-220), centred on payout reconciliation.

title: Talad Price Pulse
tagline: Crowdsourced daily ingredient prices at Talad Thai, Si Mum Mueang and Makro, with menu-cost alerts
problem: Thai restaurant and street-food margins swing with fresh ingredient prices: Thai basil doubled from 80 to 160 baht per kg after floods, vegetables rose 10-20% in early 2026, and wholesale coriander was 60-70 baht per kg while long eggplant ranged 10-30. Vendors buy at Talad Thai, Si Mum Mueang, local wet markets or Makro, but they have no easy way to compare prices across markets or know when to switch suppliers or menu items. Most only notice a cost spike when the month's cash is short, by which time a dish has been sold below cost for weeks. Official price lists are delayed and not tied to the vendor's own recipes.
solution: A LINE-first app where vendors and buyers photograph receipts or price boards; OCR extracts item, unit and price, building a near-real-time price index across major wholesale markets and Makro. Vendors enter their top recipes once, and the app recalculates plate cost daily, alerting on LINE when a dish's margin drops below target and suggesting substitutes or the cheapest market today. Contributors earn free premium access, so data grows with usage, and suppliers can pay to post offers. This differs from the food-costing content idea in the corpus (CLAUDE-240) by owning a live, crowdsourced Thai wholesale price feed.

title: Allergen Menu QR
tagline: A street vendor snaps the menu once and tourists get it in 8 languages with peanut, shrimp and gluten flags
problem: Thai menus in tourist areas often carry vague English names and no transliteration, and street stalls frequently have no English menu at all. Peanuts, shrimp paste, fish sauce, oyster sauce and soy sauce (gluten) are everywhere, so tourists with allergies either avoid street food or gamble, and travel insurers explicitly warn allergic travellers about Thailand. Vendors lose foreign customers who walk past a menu they cannot read, while a few restaurants already list allergens per dish to win them. Generic QR menus translate names but do not know which Thai dishes typically contain which allergens.
solution: The vendor photographs a menu board or speaks dish names into LINE; the app recognises the dishes, maps each to a Thai dish knowledge base of typical ingredients, and asks the vendor 3-4 tap questions to confirm (peanuts on top? shrimp paste in the paste?). It generates a printable QR and a phone-friendly menu in English, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Russian, Arabic, French and German, with photos, spice level, allergen icons and halal/jay/vegan flags. Tourists can show a Thai-language request card to the vendor (no peanuts, no fish sauce) generated from their selections. Unlike basic QR menus (IDEA-075 in the corpus), the value is the Thai dish allergen knowledge base that improves with every vendor confirmation.

competitor_gap: Camera translation renders names but not hidden ingredients; QR builders do not know Thai dish allergen profiles
demand_evidence: Travelfish notes most tourist menus lack transliteration and give vague names; travel insurers publish Thailand allergy guides warning about soy, peanuts and shellfish; some restaurants already list allergens per dish.

commoditization_risk: Medium: Google Lens translation keeps improving, but cannot know a specific vendor's recipe
regulatory_notes: Liability: allergen info must be labelled as vendor-provided with a disclaimer; not a medical guarantee

title: Wongnai Review Concierge
tagline: Replies to Wongnai, Google Maps and LINE MAN reviews in your voice and turns complaints into kitchen fixes
problem: Wongnai lists more than 300,000 Thai restaurants and has around 10 million monthly users, and Wongnai itself tells owners that replying to reviews brings customers back. Yet most small restaurant owners never reply, because reviews are spread across Wongnai, Google Maps and delivery-app ratings and responding in polite Thai takes time. Unanswered complaints about cold food or rude staff sit at the top of listings for months and new customers read them, and English reviews from tourists are ignored. Owners also miss the operational pattern behind complaints, like a slow dinner shift.

It classifies complaints by cause (taste, temperature, wait, staff, packaging, price) and time of day, and sends a weekly fix list to the kitchen. Positive reviewers get thank-you replies and, where the platform allows, a return offer. It is a Thailand-specific adaptation of the generic review-reply idea in the corpus (IDEA-033), adding Wongnai and LINE MAN coverage and Thai politeness registers.

title: Cloud Kitchen Brand Lab
tagline: Per-brand, per-app profit analytics for Thai cloud kitchens running five virtual brands from one kitchen
problem: Thai cloud kitchens and restaurants running several virtual brands (a krapao brand, a noodle brand, a dessert brand) on GrabFood, LINE MAN and ShopeeFood cannot see which brand is actually profitable, because ingredients and staff are shared and each app reports separately. Brands cannibalise each other in the same delivery radius, and owners keep marginal brands alive because they cannot isolate their contribution. Operators like Siamese Asset and CRG invested heavily in cloud kitchens, but small operators lack analysts. Prep-time and rating penalties on one brand can drag down the whole kitchen's ranking.
solution: Connects delivery-app reports and the POS or ingredient purchases, then allocates shared costs to brands by recipe usage and prep time to produce true contribution margin per brand per platform. It detects cannibalisation (orders shifting between own brands at the same address), tracks prep time and rating per brand, and recommends which brand to pause, reprice or relaunch. A test-and-learn module helps launch a new virtual brand with a small menu and reports on its first 30 days against a benchmark of similar brands. This builds on the content idea in the corpus (CLAUDE-239) by being a data product for operators.

title: Halal Supplier Verifier
tagline: B2B sourcing of CICOT-certified ingredients with certificate checks for kitchens going halal

title: Jay Vegan Supply Hub

title: Talking Daily Books
tagline: Vendors speak sales and costs into LINE in Thai and get daily profit and a bank-ready statement
problem: Thailand has about 3.28 million SMEs, most of them micro-enterprises, and street-food and market vendors are among the least documented: they keep no books, so they cannot show income to banks and fall back on informal lenders at high interest. They already take PromptPay for a growing share of sales, but cash sales and ingredient costs are never recorded, so profit is a guess. Accounting apps assume typing and accounting vocabulary, which busy vendors with flour-covered hands will not use. Banks and the BOT keep promoting SME credit access, but lenders need statements vendors do not have.

The bot replies each evening with sales, costs and profit, and a weekly trend in simple Thai. After three months the vendor can generate an income statement and cash-flow summary to share with a bank or microfinance lender, with the vendor's consent. Banks and lenders pay per qualified applicant referral, which keeps the vendor app free.

title: Slip Forensics Guard
tagline: Catches AI-edited, recycled and wrong-account transfer slips before staff hand over goods
problem: Fake transfer slips are a daily risk for Thai shops: apps sell slip generators where names, amounts and times are typed in, and in 2025 bloggers showed a chatbot could edit a real 23,000-baht slip into a 400,000-baht one with watermarks intact. Police arrested a couple in April 2026 for using doctored slips to get free petrol and meals, and online-purchase fraud is the most frequent cyber offence in Thailand. Banks advise scanning the slip QR with a bank app, but busy staff skip it, and a genuine QR can be reused from an old slip or point to someone else's account. Slip-check bots verify the reference, yet sellers still lose money to recycled slips and same-amount timing tricks.

It then waits for the matching credit to arrive in the shop's account feed where connected and only shows green when money has actually landed. Staff get a simple traffic-light result in under 5 seconds, and owners get a log of suspicious slips with payer details for police reports. The network-wide duplicate database is the moat no single-shop slip checker has.

title: Tour Chargeback Shield
tagline: Builds winning chargeback evidence for Thai hotels, tour operators and dive shops paid by foreign cards
problem: Tourism businesses in Phuket, Krabi, Koh Samui and Bangkok take foreign card payments for tours, dives and stays, and Mastercard has reported fraud in travel agencies and tour bookings at more than four times the cross-industry average. Friendly fraud is common: a guest completes the boat trip and then disputes the charge at home as not received, and the merchant has days to respond with evidence they never organised. Gateways like Omise and 2C2P provide dispute portals but not the evidence, and small operators lose disputes by default, paying the amount plus fees, while high dispute ratios threaten their merchant account. Regulators and courts have shifted liability toward banks for genuine card fraud, which makes merchants the softer target in disputes.

When a dispute arrives, it auto-assembles a reason-code-specific evidence pack in English, submits it through the gateway, and tracks the outcome. Prevention rules flag risky bookings (mismatched card country, last-minute high-value bookings) and prompt for 3-D Secure or deposits. A small fee per won dispute aligns incentives, which global chargeback tools rarely offer at Thai SME scale.
